components.note: 灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè
犭 (dog/animal) — 狗 names an animal, the dog.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to gǒu, having drifted apart over time.
马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
The character traces the head and shaft of a simple nail, a shape later borrowed for other meanings.
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
木 (tree) forms the base.
一 marks the very top of the tree, giving 末 its meaning 'end, tip, final.'
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
Rice/grain — sugar was traditionally made from grains or cane.
Gives the sound táng, matching the character's reading.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

meanings: also pr. [dai1 hui3 r5] or [dai1 hui5 r5]

components.note: 彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
玨 (two connected jade pieces, standing in for strings) shows 瑟 relates to a stringed instrument.
必 (bì) gives a sound distantly related to sè, having drifted apart over time.

meanings: variant of 諮詢|咨询[zi1 xun2]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咨 relates to speaking, asking for advice.
次 (cì) gives a sound only distantly related to zī today, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) shows 询 relates to asking or speaking.
旬 (xún) gives the exact sound of 询.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
广 depicts a roofed building or shelter.
廷 depicts an open court or hall — together with the shelter above, giving 庭 its meaning 'courtyard, hall.'
勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
囗 (an enclosure) — 围 relates to surrounding or encircling something
韦 (wéi) gives the sound — 围 is also pronounced wéi, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'
米 (grain/rice) — 糊 originally referred to a paste made from rice or grain.
胡 (hú) gives the sound — an exact match with 糊.
Water — early sense linked to a river name, later extended to smearing liquid.
Gives the sound yú, related to tú but drifted apart over time.
火 (fire) shows 燃 relates directly to burning.
然 (rán) gives the exact sound of 燃.
火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.
豕 (boar) — 豪 originally described a fierce, bristling boar-like porcupine, extending to 'heroic, grand.'
高 (gāo) shares the rhyme -ao with háo, though the initial has drifted from g- to h- over time.
十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
Hand — a fist is a closed hand.
Gives a sound distantly related to quán, having drifted apart over time.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
氵 (water) — 混 originally described muddy, mixed water.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound distantly related to hùn, having drifted apart over time.
爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
口 (mouth) — arguing is done vocally.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound fairly close to chǎo, sharing the rhyme.
车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.
山 (mountain) surrounds the character, setting the scene.
幺 (small, doubled here) shows tiny hidden niches within the mountainside, giving 幽 its meaning 'secluded, hidden, dark.'
黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
知 (to know) forms the upper part of the character.
日 (sun, clarity) — knowledge seen as clearly as the sun gave 智 its meaning 'wisdom.'
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
辶 (to walk) — 退 relates to moving backward or away
艮 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to 退's reading tuì, having drifted apart over time
囗 depicts an enclosure or fence.
木 (tree) — a tree hemmed in by a fence, unable to grow freely, gave 困 its meaning 'trapped, difficult.'
心 (heart) at the bottom shows this is about a state of mind.
或 (perhaps, maybe) above conveys uncertainty, giving 惑 its meaning 'to confuse, to be puzzled.'
弋 (a dagger-axe/weapon) — represents military force.
止 (foot/to stop) — stopping an enemy by force of arms gave 武 its meaning 'military, martial.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
辶 (to walk) — 透 relates to moving all the way through something.
秀 (xiù) gives a sound distantly related to tòu, having drifted apart over time.
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.
斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.
爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
录 traditionally depicted a hand-held tool used for carving or writing records — the image behind its meaning 'to record, to write down.'
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
心 (heart) — 恩 relates to feelings of gratitude and kindness.
因 (yīn) gives the sound — an exact match with 恩.
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'
火 (fire) — 灯 names a lamp, which once gave light through a small flame.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to dēng, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.
土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
目 (eye) — supervising, 督's meaning, involves watching closely.
叔 (shū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading dū has diverged.
辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
扌 (hand) — 举 relates to lifting or raising something with the hand
舉 (jǔ) is the traditional character's own form, giving the sound directly, an exact match
戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'
辶 (to walk) — 追 relates to moving in pursuit of someone or something
㠯 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 追's reading zhuī, having drifted apart over time
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.
氵 (water) — 淇 names a river; it appears in the name of the Qi River (淇河) in Henan.
其 (qí) gives an exact match for 淇's reading.
氵 (water) — 淋 describes water dripping or drenching something.
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 淋.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'
足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
贝 (money, from ancient shell currency) — 赖 relates to depending on someone for support, as in 'to rely on.'
剌 (là) gives a sound close to lài, sharing the initial l- and a similar rhyme.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
